//notes: Each value is the MAX acceptable lava/node wall-time ratio (lava is allowed to be up to Nx Node's time). A benchmark with no entry here is report-only (never fails the gate). Calibrated 2026-07-11 against the perf/buffer tip (observed ratio x ~1.5-2 headroom for CI noise); re-run `make bench` and tighten further as the ratios improve.

caps.//encoding: Added 2026-07-27 with bench/micro/encoding.js. The absolute ratios are high because everything except decode-utf8-fastpath is a pure-JS codec against Node's native ICU/C++ one; the caps exist to catch a REGRESSION, not to claim parity. Calibration, stated explicitly so it is not read as stronger than it is: each cap is ~1.4x the TYPICAL observed ratio on a quiet box (e.g. decode-win1252 14.0 vs a typical 10.2x). decode-win1252 and decode-utf8-stream were widened on 2026-07-28 from 11.5/17.0 after they tripped on machine noise alone - a loaded box produced 12.9x/18.4x while a paired per-process A/B of the very same two builds showed 0.995x on both. Against those worst-case loaded readings the headroom is only ~1.03-1.08x. So: with run-to-run noise reaching ~1.27x, these caps CANNOT reliably catch the ~1.43x regression that motivated them - they are a coarse backstop against something much larger, and the real guard is a paired per-process A/B against the previous build (min and median over >=9 launches, one benchmark per process).
